title: The Cosmic Steering Wheel NGC 1269
caption: The barred spiral galaxy NGC 1269, imaged by the Dark Energy Camera on the Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope
celestial: NGC 1269 · constellation Eridanus · about 33 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: Dark Energy Survey/DOE/FNAL/DECam/CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA. Image processing: R. Colombari & M. Zamani (NSF NOIRLab)

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A bar slices through the centre of NGC 1269, and inner and outer disks form wheel-like rings around its core, earning it the title the Cosmic Steering Wheel. NGC 1269 is an early-type spiral galaxy in the constellation Eridanus, some 33 million light-years from Earth.

Bars are common features in spiral galaxies. The rings in NGC 1269 are thought to have formed after NGC 1269 merged with another galaxy, while the inner disk is believed to have been shaped further by density waves spreading outward from the galaxy's centre. Density waves are zones of slightly higher density that travel through a galaxy's disk, squeezing gas and stars as they pass.

The data were drawn from the Dark Energy Survey's archive, a project which the Department of Energy and NSF operated between 2013 and 2019 using the specially designed Dark Energy Camera (DECam). The survey imaged hundreds of millions of galaxies, and today DECam is open to other scientists on the Blanco telescope.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (29.31 x 29.33 arcminutes) and distance (33 million light years), the frame spans roughly 281,000 × 282,000 light-years. Its light set out about 33 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Taken with DECam on the Blanco 4-meter Telescope through g and r filters. The colour mapping isn't published.
